Mundlak (correlated random effects) device

Source: R/panel.R
mundlak.Rd

Augments a data frame with the unit-level means of the numeric case-specific covariates in the formula (every part of a multipart formula; in the long layout only variables that are constant within a case are averaged, over the unit's cases), and returns the augmented formula and data. A covariate constant within every unit is not averaged (it is its own unit mean; its coefficient is the between-unit effect), with a message. Fitting remnl() on the result implements the Mundlak / correlated-random-effects specification: the coefficients on the original covariates are the within-unit effects while those on the means capture (and test) the correlation between the covariates and the unit effect, without the incidental-parameters bias of unit dummies in short panels. A pooled mnl() fit of the augmented formula with cluster = "unit" is the population-averaged version: its slopes are attenuated towards zero by the unit-effect variance (in the vignette's example by about a quarter), as in any nonlinear model, and are consistent for average effects, not for the within-unit coefficients.

Usage

mundlak(formula, data, unit, id = NULL, weights = NULL, suffix = "_mean")

Arguments

formula

A model formula, possibly with | parts.

data

A data frame.

unit

Column name identifying the unit.

id

Long layout: the case column (so that each case counts once in the unit mean); NULL for the wide layout.

weights

Optional frequency weights (a column name or a vector aligned to the rows of data); the unit means are then weighted means, as the fit will be.

suffix

Suffix of the added mean columns (default "_mean").

Value

A list with formula (the augmented formula, keeping the | structure), data, and added (the names of the mean columns).

References

Mundlak, Y. (1978). On the pooling of time series and cross section data. Econometrica, 46, 69-85. doi:10.2307/1913646

See also

mnl(), imnl(); the fe and cluster arguments of the estimators.

Examples

## 40 units of 15 cases; each unit's effect on alternative b is
## correlated with its mean of x1
set.seed(1)
unit <- rep(1:40, each = 15); u <- rnorm(40)
x1 <- rnorm(600) + u[unit]; x2 <- rnorm(600)
V <- cbind(0, 0.5 - x1 + 0.8 * x2 + u[unit], -0.3 + 0.6 * x1 - 0.5 * x2)
y <- apply(exp(V) / rowSums(exp(V)), 1, function(p) sample(c("a", "b", "c"), 1, prob = p))
d <- data.frame(y = factor(y), x1, x2, unit)
m <- mundlak(y ~ x1 + x2, d, unit = "unit")
m$formula
#> y ~ x1 + x2 + x1_mean + x2_mean
#> <environment: 0x5de62a803248>
fit <- mnl(m$formula, m$data, cluster = "unit")
## the unit mean of x1 picks up the unit effect in b's equation; without
## the means x1's slope absorbs it. This pooled fit estimates average
## effects: its x1 slope is close to the within-unit -1 of the simulation
## only because the unit mean takes up nearly all of the unit effect here
## (15 cases per unit). remnl() on m$formula estimates the within-unit
## coefficients.
coef(fit)[grep("x1", names(coef(fit)))]
#>       b:x1  b:x1_mean       c:x1  c:x1_mean 
#> -1.0542526  0.7851798  0.5203237 -0.1141086 
coef(mnl(y ~ x1 + x2, d, cluster = "unit"))[c("b:x1", "c:x1")]
#>       b:x1       c:x1 
#> -0.6107817  0.4668951
